location: Menlo Park, California — Convent of the Sacred Heart
year: c. 1911–1922 (undated and never mailed; written "July 16," and a note mentions "Saturday the 22nd," which fits 1911, 1916 or 1922)
recipient: Miss Anne Hanna, 37 Park View[?] (no city given)
notes: Front: "Convent of the Sacred Heart, Menlo Park, California. View of West and South Wings.", a sepia view of the convent's mansard-roofed wing with a rounded corner tower and a cupola, half hidden behind palms and framed by a huge oak. The Religious of the Sacred Heart opened the convent school in 1898; the grounds became part of Atherton when it incorporated in 1923, and the school continues today as Sacred Heart Schools. Back: divided back with a rose ornament; no stamp and no postmark (just an "X" in the stamp box), so it was probably hand-delivered or sent in an envelope. The writer appears to be a guest at the convent who plans to return to Seattle. The main message runs crosswise to the address. Two extra notes are squeezed around the address: "I expect to return to 2700 Jackson at the end of the week —" and, upside down beside the stamp box, "I am to return to 2700[?] Jackson on Saturday the 22nd." Several names are hard to read and flagged. Message: "July 16 — Last Monday I came here with Mme. Wille[?], Mgr. Cantwell[?] and Norma Bourbon[?]. It was indeed a lovely ride[?] — we came through the Presidio and had several beautiful sights of the Golden Gate. But you would scarcely[?] know the place, as well[?]. To-morrow the Novena for the Feast of St. Anne will begin. Be assured you will be included in mine. Keep me in yours. I hope to see you before I start back for Seattle. Miss Conley[?] is lovely. Kindest love to all from Aunt Anne" (The novena to St. Anne traditionally starts July 17 and ends on her feast day, July 26, which fits "To-morrow" on July 16.) A pencil dealer mark ("527.50") is on the address side.

feed_description: An aunt staying at the Convent of the Sacred Heart in Menlo Park writes to her namesake niece: a drive through the Presidio past the Golden Gate, and a novena to St. Anne starting tomorrow.

location: Jerusalem — The Old City from the Mount of Olives
year: c. early 1970s (dated Oct. 13; postmark: Jerusalem, Cheshvan, 15.10[?] — year not legible)
sender: Cathy B. (a niece, studying abroad with a group)
recipient: Mrs. Mary E. Andrus, 7855 Willow Hill Court No. 3[?]2, Dallas, Texas 75230, U.S.A.
notes: Front: "Jerusalem, Old City", seen from the Mount of Olives: the golden Dome of the Rock and the Old City walls, the onion domes of the Russian Church of Mary Magdalene in the middle distance, the Dormition Abbey on the horizon at left, and a man plowing a hillside field with a mule in the foreground. Back: "General view of the Old City of Jerusalem from Mt. of Olives" (also in French); copyright by Palphot, printed in the Holy Land (no. 9851). Two Israeli stamps, a 0.10 Bet She'an town emblem and a 0.70 En Gedi landscape, the latter apparently from the landscape definitives of the early 1970s. The Jerusalem postmark gives the Hebrew month (Cheshvan) and a date that looks like 15.10; the year is not legible. Marked "AIRMAIL." The greeting "Aunt Betty" suggests Betty is a nickname for the addressee. Message: "Oct. 13. Dear Aunt Betty, Our group has been here in Jerusalum for almost two weeks now, and even though Israel kinda reminds me of Phoenix — I love it here! There's so much value to there culture, I wish I understood it better. As a group we've traveled all over the place — studying as we go, and have spent a lot of time inside the old city of Jerusalum as well. Some of the best times I've had here were when just a few of us would wander around the old city shops & sites. We stay another week, have a final or two, then we'll leave for Greece. I loved England & Scotland. We also spent some time in Cairo and a couple days in Jordan. I'm really learning a lot — wishing I could learn more — but I'm getting so smart that my wisdom teeth are coming in!! Sending love to you, Cathy B." Added at the bottom: "Hi to my cousin & new cousin-in-law too!!" A dealer sticker ("#1843 CARD $0.49") is on the address side.
feed_description: A student on a study-abroad tour writes from Jerusalem: Israel reminds her of Phoenix, but she loves it, and she's getting so smart her wisdom teeth are coming in.

year: c. 1970s (postmark: Granada[?], June — year digits unclear)
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. T. C. Barnes & Family, 5501 Gloucester, Austin, Texas, U.S. 78723
notes: Front: the Puerta de Alcalá at night, floodlit, with streaks of traffic light around it; the attic inscription reads "REGE CAROLO III ANNO MDCCLXXVIII" (in the reign of Charles III, 1778). Back: "326.— Madrid, Puerta de Alcala"; published by J. L. Gallegos, Madrid. A 15-peseta stamp honoring the architect Secundino Zuazo. The machine slogan cancel reminds senders that letters for Madrid and Barcelona must carry the postal district number. The circular postmark is only partly legible (it appears to read Granada), dated June, with an unclear year. Message: "Dearest Faye, Buddy & Family: You just can't imagine what a beautiful country Spain is and we're having a wonderful time. Donna is our guide. She speaks like a native and understands the customs of the country. She has reserved rooms in beautiful hotels for us in each town we plan to tour. The car we have engaged is a Renault. She handles it like a cowboy riding a bronk. People here drive like mad. I'm enjoying every minute — We don't get to bed before 2:00–3:00 A.M. Will have lots to tell you. Love Mom" A dealer sticker ("1843 $0.49") is on the address side; it matches the Jerusalem card and came from the same dealer lot.
feed_description: Mom writes home to Austin from Spain: Donna is their guide, speaks like a native and drives the rented Renault "like a cowboy riding a bronk," and nobody gets to bed before 2 or 3 A.M.
